dedupe_keys.name: microsoft building damage assessment toolkits satellite imagery and damage proxy maps

description: Two Microsoft repositories give tools for assessing building damage after disasters from remote sensing. The building-damage-assessment toolkit fine-tunes a damage model end to end, with a labelling tool, scripts to make segmentation masks, training and inference, and was used for the 2023 Turkey and Syria earthquakes and the 2023 tornadoes in Rolling Fork, Mississippi; it also analyses damage proxy maps made from pre- and post-event SAR coherence by NASA JPL's ARIA project and the Earth Observatory of Singapore. The siamese CNN repository, a Microsoft AI for Humanitarian Action project with the Netherlands Red Cross 510 initiative, segments building footprints and classifies each building's damage, trained on the public xBD dataset, and runs in Docker. Coverage: any area with suitable imagery. Access: free on GitHub. Licence: MIT. Caveats: models need local fine-tuning and labels for new events. Simulation uses are rapid post-event damage estimates that feed shelter needs, recovery modelling and validation of fragility curves. Related records: the Microsoft AI for Good building damage assessments on HDX.
inputs: Pre- and post-event satellite or aerial imagery
SAR damage proxy maps (e.g. from NASA JPL ARIA)
